context.text: What this study tests & key takeaways: We evaluated 9 open-weight models across 3 model families — Google Gemma 4 (E4B, 12B, 26B), Alibaba Qwen 3 (4B, 9B, 14B), and Meta Llama 3.x / Hermes 3 (3.2B, 8B, Hermes 3 8B) — across 3 pathways at an 8k chart budget: (1) Direct AI (condensed chart only), (2) Direct + Clinical KB (chart + Stage-2 4-Layer KB rules), and (3) Med Agent Hub (chart + clinical rules + patient entity-relationship subgraph + Tier-0 overflow recovery), spanning 36 clinical accuracy & conversational privacy scenarios on 10 complex patients (972 total cells, graded by blinded Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 judges). Key Finding 1 — Gemma 4 is the clear leader for single-model clinical synthesis, sweeping the top 7 of all 27 setups (67.2–82.1/100 vs. 65.4/100 for the best Qwen 3 14B setup and 55.3/100 for the best Llama 3.1 8B setup), with zero fabricated or unsupported citations across all 216 Gemma 4 12B and 26B answers. Gemma 4 12B + Med Agent Hub (80.5/100) is the practical single-model sweet spot — within 1.6 points of Gemma 4 26B + Hub (82.1/100) while achieving the lowest unsafe-answer rate (2/36, −71% vs. Direct 12B) and lowest confabulation count (1/36) in the sweep — while compact Gemma 4 E4B (4B eff.) + Hub (70.4/100) beats both raw Gemma 4 12B (67.2/100) and Qwen 3 14B + Hub (65.4/100). Key Finding 2 — Across every model ≥ 4B across all three families, Med Agent Hub monotonically boosts benchmark scores and cuts unsafe answers by 33%–71% over Direct AI, while 3.2B (Llama 3.2 3B) marks the capability floor below which dense multi-clinic + rule context overwhelms the model.
